cause: Elowen's letter is dated about sixteen years back, so 'dead thirty years' only works if counted from some other date; the DM never worked out when the boy died and just picked a round number.

The DM had ruled the assize falls on the 30th but kept a wrong 'twentieth' in mind and did not subtract Day 13 from 30, so it said about a week and a half instead of 17 days; the notebook only said 'month's end', not the 30th.

The shown Bait Wagon quest still said 'eight Vantry guards' (the total the arbiter could spare), and the DM used that total for the guards in the reeds instead of the six it had said two replies earlier.
In one reply it wrote 'Three bandits still stand' and then 'two with scimitars and two with crossbows', after the previous reply had correctly said four were left.
Guard distance was never tracked; the guards were 'a round away' for several rounds and the DM re-guessed the distance each time (twenty paces, then thirty) instead of keeping it shrinking.

The DM took up the player's bluff of 'eight guards/crossbows' as fact and the shown quest note also said eight, although it had said Pell and six guards, and ends this very reply with 'Pell and six guards'.
Guards were described as carrying crossbows and short swords earlier, but the notebook held no weapon detail and the DM improvised 'spears' when narrating the melee.
It repeated the bluffed 'eight crossbows' from the player's own line and the previous reply, rather than the six guards plus Pell it had in the notebook.

Ansel's lamp backstory (grandsire gave it to the Lantern-Bearer) was invented on the spot in R138 and sits awkwardly with 'your mother took the lamp from me'; the notebook had none of the earlier wording and Ansel is meant to be an unreliable speaker.
The closing summary line says 'a camp under a grey sky' and the next sentence says the first stars are coming out; a careless wording clash inside one paragraph.

The DM said 'a day's ride to Thornhallow' without adding up the distances it had already ruled (Saltmarsh to Marrowford four days, Thornhallow a day below Marrowford); the four-day figure was never put in the notebook.
The tool line showed 1d20 [10] + 2 = 12 and the DM narrated 11, misreading or mis-adding the roll.
Pell had six guards and sent two back to Saltmarsh, so four were left, but the DM sent five riders in one list without counting; the notebook was right but that entry was not shown this round.
In the same reply Kit and Wren are the two at the gate (Pell is calling for buckets), then 'all three of you at the gate' appears, a miscount of who is present.
Only three of Sparrow's shots (R147, R148, R149) had missed Wren but the DM said four times running; shot counts are not kept anywhere, so it was estimated.

The DM made up a gossip clue (Sparrow buying a horse at dusk on Day 16 with a stiff arm) without checking that Sparrow was at the barn fight at 10:30 PM that night; the notebook had the fight time but the entry was not shown.
Pell's count of guards was never updated after two went to Saltmarsh and others rode out, so he is made to say 'six spears' (and 'six tired guards' later) from the original number.

The DM had ruled Saltmarsh to Marrowford at four days with Thornhallow a day short of that, but quoted 'five days' for the trip to Saltmarsh from Thornhallow/Marrowford without redoing the sum; the Thornhallow note with the figures was not shown.

The player's own plan said the prisoners would follow behind, and the DM kept that picture even though Edric had agreed to hold Ansel in the manor and ride with him on the 29th; the two plans were never reconciled.

Tam's note said Harrow would sail at the Day 18 dawn ebb, then the tally-sheet clue invented a full payment and a hold until the 24th; it could be read as a later change but the DM never marked it as one.
The notebook and the dialogue said Hale came twelve years ago on Oake's letter, but the DM wrote that Aldous wrote 'eleven years ago' and then sent Hale; a year was dropped when restating.
Oake dictated and Wren wrote the statement but he signed it, so the DM comparing 'his own hand' on it is loosely worded rather than clearly wrong; no one ever said who wrote the body.
Kit was said to be 'forty paces' behind Wren in R177 and R179, and the DM turned that into 'forty feet' (a roughly third of the distance), mixing units.
